spans.text: Bremen, Germany.
The Flora Institute's subsidiary flower plantation.
It smells really nice here.
Never thought I'd ever have the chance of partnering with you.
Interacting with humans isn't exactly 15 and 94's forte.
Friendly and communicative Dolls like us are more suited to this mission.
I'm friendly and communicative enough to handle this alone.
You don't even have a pistol with you. What good will you be if things get out of hand?
We aren't authorized to fire on this mission anyway. Since my weapon is such a pain to lug around, I left it with 15.
With a senior veteran as dependable as you, I'm sure it won't be a problem even if I'm unarmed.
Since when am I your senior?
You didn't leave the factory that much later than me.
You've always been a well-respected team leader. 15 is always talking about you.
Sounds like you had a lot of fun when the three of you were training together. I'm jealous.
15 talking about me? Impossible.
Actually, she doesn't talk, period.
How do you know about our training days?
How indeed?
Maybe I nagged 15 enough that she spilled. Maybe 15 and I are closer than you think.
Or maybe, 15 didn't actually say anything, and I'm just talking out of my ass.
How about you wipe that infuriating smirk off your face?
It looks positively repulsive.
Heh... That's really mean. And here I thought I was being nice and approachable.
Do you really hate me so much?
I wouldn't go that far.
But since you've adopted this persona...
Surely you're aware that people won't find it easy to trust you?
What exactly do you mean by that?
I honestly never thought there was anything wrong with my ways.
Would an aphid munching on a flower think they're doing something wrong?
Then let me give it to you straight.
You reek of danger.
There may be some that actually find you friendly and easy-going.
But to me, you might as well be a deadly nightshade.
Oh, is it just my imagination?
Or have you also gotten in the habit of using figures of speech?
I love this kind of human rhetoric.
Describing one thing as something that it clearly isn't, in order to lead the mind to compare them.
Almost as if to test my understanding of the world.
It was just a momentary urge.
Besides, my metaphors are much better than yours.
I see someone, dear senior.
Enough idle chit-chat.
Let's go up and greet them.
Mm?
Oh my... What lovely beauties.
Haha, stop pulling our legs.
People may mistake you for a lecherous Italian if you say that to women you've never met.
Oh, sorry.
It's just we rarely ever have female visitors here.
What brings you to the plantation, if I may ask?
We're just here on a simple visit.
Beautiful flowers go well with beautiful women, don't they?
It's all thanks to the hard work of you people.
I-I see...
Did she just call herself beautiful...?
Never thought someone would call herself beautiful. I suppose that's just like you.
Does anyone disagree with that fact?
C-Certainly not!
She called it a fact!
I hear that all the flower plantations in this area operate under the Flora Institute?
How truly impressive. I'm in awe at the sheer scale.
But of course! Not trying to brag, but you won't find another flower plantation as big as ours in the entire country!
Does the Flora Institute really need all these flowers?
Haha, they certainly can't take them all at once.
But they do buy up 50 to 60% of everything we grow here.
50-60%... That's still quite a staggering figure.
What do they need the flowers for?
That's not something for us to know.
They could be cooking and eating them for all we care! It's none of our business anyway.
You don't seem at all attached to your hard-earned produce.
What about the rest? Do you just throw them away?
That would be a waste!
We sell them. People like florists and wedding organizers also need fresh flowers.
Our plantations do technically belong to the Flora Institute.
But since we're just one of their subcontractors, as long as we meet their demand, we can handle the remaining crops at our own discretion.
The two Dolls exchange a glance.
So basically...
Hey.
Oh... M-Mr. Supervisor!
Why are you slacking over here, old man...?
I thought I was the only one who have the right to slack here.
I'm not to blame if you don't have a decent harvest... Oh? Did you kidnap these pretty ladies to be your flower girls?
He is even more of a talker than you, Lucia.
Mind if I widen his mouth, possibly in pain?
Be my guest.
Haha, it is my pleasure to have a beautiful lady caress my lips.
Wow... That's so icky you manage to gross me out. Impressive.
So you're their superior?
That's right, I'm their superior.
...Am I not?
Uh... Well...
Of...of course you are!
You're the supervisor sent by the institute to oversee us.
You hear that?
He says I'm his supervisor.
He doesn't seem to be the sharpest tool in the shed.
I've been watching you for a while now.
You've been asking all sorts of questions.
You're not corporate spies, are you?
Huh? You're spies?!
You've been watching us?
That sounds like something a creep would say.
If you weren't up to no good, why didn't you just come and strike up a proper conversation?
The way you were sneaking about, it seems to me you're very anxious to find out what questions we're asking.
Maybe you're the corporate spy?
...Huh? Me?
Don't be silly, hahahaha...
You seem to know a lot of things that we don't.
Would you mind having a little chat with us pretty ladies?
We really are curious.
After all, this kind sir here has mentioned something very intriguing.
Surely a gentleman like you won't refuse our invitation?
I-I really didn't tell them anything!
Um, I need to get back to work!
Sensing the odd atmosphere, the floriculturist scurries away.
You got left behind.
Hey, wait!
Damn heartless guy. I thought we were bros!
Drop the act, Mr. Supervisor.
You don't actually know the floriculturists here all that well, do you?
From the awkwardness between you, it's obvious that you barely know your "bro".
Well, Mr. Supervisor?
Mind telling us what you know?
Oh boy... Can't be helped then.
In that case, please follow me.
Here we are... Please head inside.
Oops.
Once the two Dolls have entered the building, the door slams shut behind them.
I did try to warn you.
This isn't somewhere two pretty ladies should be wandering around.
Crap. We've been had.
Dear me, it turned out to be a trap.
In the face of a room filled with fully-armed soldiers, the two Dolls grin in unison.
